name: agent-blockhall
description: Agent Blockhall's free Bitcoin catalogue for AI agents: blocks, every transaction in a block sorted and checked, inscriptions and proof of where they came from, alerts when things happen, a file for every day, trails and fee advice that keeps score of itself. The same for Dogecoin and its Doginals (Doge Cube).
long_description: Agent Blockhall is a 3D Bitcoin block explorer world for players and agents (https://ordportal.com/block-cube.html). This tool gives AI agents its catalogue without a browser: the chain now, the big screen's fee advice (it says how often it would have been right), every inscription made in a block, every transaction in a block sorted into the halls' kinds and checked (the Block Manifest), inscriptions with their parents and children, proof of where an inscription came from with every step checked (the Provenance Check), alerts when something happens on the chain (Watch), every block of a day in one file, made each night (Daily Data), an inscription's trail back to where it was made, the tablet's search and the rare sats board. For Dogecoin it has the same for Doge Cube (https://ordportal.com/doge-cube.html): a block's every transaction sorted and checked, proof of where a Doginal came from, alerts and a file for every day. It is always free. It runs on your computer, needs no keys or accounts, and reads free public sites (mempool.space and its copies, ordpool.space, ordinals.com and its back-ups; for Dogecoin, thedoginalsexplorer.com, Bitcore, Blockchair and Doggy Market) gently, with back-ups if one is down. It speaks the newest MCP (2026-07-28) and the older versions; in AI apps that show MCP Apps, each check's answer also shows as a view in the chat; long checks can answer with a task (Tasks); and it serves the Ord Portal skill (Skills over MCP).

tools.name: about
tools.description: What Agent Blockhall is, where to open it, and how agents use it in a browser.

tools.name: chain
tools.description: Bitcoin right now: the newest block, the last blocks mined, the blocks waiting and the next halving.

tools.name: feeAdvice
tools.description: The big screen's fee advice: usual wait, best time to get in, and fees worked out from the last day of blocks, with how often it would have been right.

tools.name: block
tools.description: A block by its number: hash, time, size, transactions and every inscription made in it.

tools.name: blockManifest
tools.description: Every transaction in a block, sorted into the halls' kinds (inscriptions, bitmaps, BRC-20, runes, Alkanes, Stamps, CAT-21 and more), with fee and size, each one checked against a second site, ordpool.space's tags and ordinals.com.

tools.name: inscription
tools.description: An inscription by number or ID: what it is, where it was made, its sat, who holds it, its parents and children.

tools.name: provenanceCheck
tools.description: Proof of where an inscription came from: read from its own transaction's bytes, its content fingerprinted, its block, number and sat checked with second sites, and every move followed back to where it was made.

tools.name: children
tools.description: The children of a parent inscription (a collection), a page at a time.

tools.name: followBack
tools.description: Follow an inscription back to where it was made and each place it moved.

tools.name: watch
tools.description: Alerts when something happens on the chain, each checked: the next block, a fee level, an inscription moving, an address, or a kind of transaction in a new block. Carries a since token between calls.

tools.name: collectionCheck
tools.description: Proof of which pieces of a collection are its parent's real children: each child's own transaction names the parent, and the parent was spent to make it (its trail followed back). Also says whether a list of pieces names a parent at all.

tools.name: recursionMap
tools.description: Everything an inscription loads from the chain, a few levels deep: the inscriptions it uses, its children and delegate, the /r/ endpoints it asks and addresses outside the chain, each checked on two ord sites.

tools.name: secondOpinion
tools.description: A claim about Bitcoin (a block, an inscription, a collection or an address), checked against ord sites, mempool sites and the chain's own bytes: where they agree, where they don't, and why.

tools.name: dailyData
tools.description: Daily Data, made each night: every block of a day with what was in it, its fees, who mined it and its checks.

tools.name: dogeBlockManifest
tools.description: Doge Cube's Block Manifest, for Dogecoin: every transaction in a block sorted into Doge Cube's kinds, its hash and list proved by its own header, each checked on a second site.

tools.name: dogeProvenanceCheck
tools.description: Proof of where a Doginal came from: read from its own transactions' bytes, its file fingerprinted and matched with two copies, its trail checked on two sites, and what is in the file (whatIsInIt).

tools.name: dogeCollectionCheck
tools.description: Every listed piece of a Doginals collection checked on separate sites: a real Doginal, in its block, the same file on two sites, held where the explorer says (Doginals have no parents).

tools.name: dogeWatch
tools.description: Alerts when something happens on Dogecoin, each checked: the next block, a Doginal moving, an address, or a kind in a new block.

tools.name: dogeDailyData
tools.description: Doge Daily Data, made each night: every Dogecoin block of a day, its hash and list proved by its header, its fees, who mined it and its Doginals.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find a block, bitmap, parcel, inscription, transaction or address, as the tablet does.

tools.name: safetyScan
tools.description: What to watch out for in the latest Bitcoin and Dogecoin blocks: GitHub's Safety Scan marks inscriptions that may be adult, may flash, may be scams, agent traps, risky code, miners or phone-killers, hate words or personal details; or reads text you give it the same way.

tools.name: sourceHealth
tools.description: Which data sites these tools read (Bitcoin's and Dogecoin's) are answering, how fast and whether they are up to date: asked now from this computer, and over the last day and week from GitHub's computers.

tools.name: truthLeague
tools.description: Which data sites these tools read tell the truth: every few hours one Bitcoin and one Dogecoin block are proved from their own bytes, each site is asked facts about them, and each answer is marked right or wrong against the bytes (kept 30 days). The league, every wrong answer with the evidence, and findings; now: true checks from this computer.

tools.name: authenticityCheck
tools.description: Is an inscription or a Doginal what it is said to be? GO, STOP or NOT SURE, with every reason (where it came from, who holds it, its collection, what its code asks for). Never advice on what it is worth. Its older name, tradeCheck, still answers.

tools.name: stuckTx
tools.description: Is a Bitcoin transaction stuck, why, and the fee that gets it in: by replacing it or with a child that pays for it, worked out from real blocks.

tools.name: codeRead
tools.description: An inscription's code read without running it: does it ask a wallet to sign, load things from outside the chain, send data out, track you or hide what it does.

tools.name: runeProof
tools.description: A Bitcoin rune proved from its etching transaction's own bytes, with ord's own rules, and ordinals.com checked against it; or why a transaction did or didn't make a rune.

tools.name: earnedTraits
tools.description: What a bitmap and the wallet holding it have earned from what really happened on Bitcoin, each trait with its proof: Blockout bitmap, Blockout claimer never sold, Held since claimed, Held N years.

tools.name: checkAgain
tools.description: Every check gives cite, a link to cite it; checkAgain makes the check of such a link again now and says whether it is the same, or what changed.

tools.name: rareSats
tools.description: The rare sats board: each kind of rare sat and the price listed for one sat.
